newsitem.title: CHINA: EXPERTS PREDICT STABLE RISE FOR CHINA STOCKS-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: EXPERTS PREDICT STABLE RISE FOR CHINA STOCKS-PAPER.

text.p: A Chinese newspaper on Tuesday quoted experts as predicting a stable rise in domestic share prices in the second half of the year, the first such show of official optimism since a May crackdown on overheating markets.
Participants at a seminar on securities prospects in the second half had concluded that share prices would be "slowly bullish", the official Financial News said.

Stock prices were closely linked to macroeconomic growth and the economy was expected to grow at a relatively fast rate in the last six months of 1997, it quoted the experts as saying, but gave no details.

Chinese officials and state media have been wary of sounding upbeat about the stock markets since May, when Beijing moved to rein in prices that had surged about 50 percent in the previous four months.

State banks and enterprises and listed firms were banned from trading stocks while the stamp duty on share purchases was raised. The measures helped to prompt prices to fall about 20 percent by early August.
